definitions.english: A bank is a safe place to keep your money.
definitions.sesotho: Banka ke sebaka se sireletsehileng sa ho boloka chelete.

definitions.english: Banks help you store, get, and send money.
definitions.sesotho: Libanka li u thusa ho boloka, ho fumana le ho romella chelete.

definitions.english: A bank account is like a special box at the bank for your money.
definitions.sesotho: Akhaonto ea banka e tshoana le lebokose le kgethehileng bankeng bakeng sa chelete ea hao.

definitions.english: Money in a bank is safe from getting lost.
definitions.sesotho: Chelete bankeng e sireletsehile hore e se lahlehe.

definitions.english: Banks are buildings where people keep money safe.
definitions.sesotho: Libanka ke meaho eo batho ba bolokang chelete ho eona.

definitions.english: Banks accept deposits, provide loans, and offer payment services.
definitions.sesotho: Libanka li amohela depositi, li fana ka likoloto le litshebeletso tsa litefo.

definitions.english: A bank account stores money securely and earns interest.
definitions.sesotho: Akhaonto ea banka e boloka chelete ka mokhoa o sireletsehileng le ho fumana phaello.

definitions.english: Banking services include savings, mobile banking, and ATMs.
definitions.sesotho: Litshebeletso tsa banka li kenyelletsa poloko, mobile banking le li-ATM.

definitions.english: Banks act as intermediaries between savers and borrowers.
definitions.sesotho: Libanka li sebetsa e le mokena-dipakeng pakeng tsa ba bolokang le ba alimang.

definitions.english: Mobile banking enables transactions through your phone.
definitions.sesotho: Mobile banking e dumella ditransakshene ka fono ea hao.

definitions.english: Banks operate under fractional reserve banking.
definitions.sesotho: Libanka li sebetsa tlasa fractional reserve banking.

definitions.english: The Central Bank of Lesotho regulates commercial banks.
definitions.sesotho: Banka e Kgolo ea Lesotho e laola libanka tsa kgwebo.

definitions.english: Banking services include deposits, credit, payments, and wealth management.
definitions.sesotho: Litshebeletso tsa banka li kenyelletsa depositi, mokitlane, litefo le taolo ea maruo.

definitions.english: Digital banking and mobile money expand financial inclusion.
definitions.sesotho: Digital banking le mobile money li eketsa ho kenyelletsoa litabeng tsa lichelete.

definitions.english: Understanding fees and rates is essential for personal finance.
definitions.sesotho: Ho utloisisa litefiso le liphaello ho bohlokwa bakeng sa lichelete tsa botho.

examples.english: Put M50 in the bank. It stays safe.
examples.sesotho: Kenya M50 bankeng. E lula e sireletsehile.

examples.english: Your parents have a bank account.
examples.sesotho: Batswadi ba hao ba na le akhaonto ea banka.

examples.english: When you take money from the bank, it is a withdrawal.
examples.sesotho: Ha u nka chelete bankeng, ke withdrawal.

examples.english: A piggy bank at home is like a mini bank!
examples.sesotho: Piggy bank lapeng e tshoana le banka e nyane!

examples.english: Banks give you a card to get your money.
examples.sesotho: Libanka li u fa karete ea ho fumana chelete ea hao.

examples.english: Open a savings account with M100. Deposit M50 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Bula akhaonto ea poloko ka M100. Kenya M50 ka khoeli.

examples.english: Use mobile banking to check balance and transfer money.
examples.sesotho: Sebelisa mobile banking ho hlahloba balance le ho romella chelete.

examples.english: Withdraw M200 from ATM using your card and PIN.
examples.sesotho: Ntsha M200 ho ATM ka karete le PIN ea hao.

examples.english: Student accounts may offer lower fees.
examples.sesotho: Liakhaonto tsa baithuti li ka fana ka litefiso tse tlase.

examples.english: Deposit part-time earnings into your bank account.
examples.sesotho: Kenya moputso oa mosebetsi oa nakwana akhaontong ea hao ea banka.

examples.english: Bank A charges M20 monthly with 3 percent interest. Bank B has no fee but 1.5 percent.
examples.sesotho: Banka A e lefisa M20 ka khoeli ka 3%. Banka B ha e lefise empa 1.5%.

examples.english: M-Pesa offers convenience but may have higher transfer fees.
examples.sesotho: M-Pesa e fana ka bonolo empa e ka ba le litefiso tse phahameng tsa ho romella.

examples.english: Fixed deposit M10,000 at 7 percent for 12 months = M700 interest.
examples.sesotho: Fixed deposit ea M10,000 ka 7% likhoeli tse 12 = M700 phaello.

examples.english: Overdraft M500 at 15 percent for 30 days = approximately M6.25 interest.
examples.sesotho: Overdraft ea M500 ka 15% matsatsi a 30 = M6.25 phaello.
Two-factor authentication e sireletsa akhaonto ea hao.

misconceptions.english: Banks keep your money in a special box — FALSE! They track it digitally.
misconceptions.sesotho: Libanka li boloka chelete ka lebokoseng — HA SE NNETE! Li e latela ka dijithale.

misconceptions.english: Only rich people use banks — FALSE! Anyone can open an account.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke barui feela ba sebelisang libanka — HA SE NNETE! Motho e mong le e mong a ka bula akhaonto.

misconceptions.english: Banks are dangerous — FALSE! They are very safe.
misconceptions.sesotho: Libanka li kotsi — HA SE NNETE! Li sireletsehile haholo.

misconceptions.english: You need lots of money to open an account — FALSE! Many start with M50.
misconceptions.sesotho: U hloka chelete e ngata ho bula akhaonto — HA SE NNETE! Tse ngata li qala ka M50.

misconceptions.english: ATMs give free money — FALSE! You withdraw what is yours.
misconceptions.sesotho: Li-ATM li fana ka chelete ea mahala — HA SE NNETE! U ntsha seo e leng sa hao.

misconceptions.english: Bank cards equal credit cards — FALSE! Debit uses your money.
misconceptions.sesotho: Likarete tsa banka li tshoana le tsa mokitlane — HA SE NNETE! Debit e sebelisa chelete ea hao.

misconceptions.english: All bank accounts are the same — FALSE! Fees and rates vary.
misconceptions.sesotho: Liakhaonto tsohle tsa banka lia tshoana — HA SE NNETE! Litefiso le liphaello lia fapana.

misconceptions.english: Banks do not charge for accounts — FALSE! Many charge monthly fees.
misconceptions.sesotho: Libanka ha li lefise liakhaonto — HA SE NNETE! Tse ngata li lefisa khoeli le khoeli.

misconceptions.english: Money in bank is 100 percent risk-free — FALSE! Very safe but not absolute.
misconceptions.sesotho: Chelete bankeng ha e na kotsi — HA SE NNETE! E sireletsehile empa eseng ka ho phethahala.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know how to open a bank account?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u batla ho tseba ho bula akhaonto ea banka?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about keeping money safe?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka ho boloka chelete e sireletsehile?
Na u batla ho utloisisa mobile banking?
Na re bapise liakhaonto tsa banka?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn about saving in a bank?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u batla ho ithuta ka ho boloka bankeng?

how_to.english: Ask your parents to open a bank account for you.
how_to.sesotho: Kopa batswadi ho u bulela akhaonto.

how_to.english: Deposit money in the bank to keep it safe.
Learn to use an ATM with adult supervision.
how_to.sesotho: Ithute ho sebelisa ATM le motho e moholo.

how_to.english: Compare bank accounts before choosing one.
Set up mobile banking on your phone.
Understand fees and minimum balance requirements.
Explore fixed deposits for higher interest.

why.english: Banks keep your money safe from theft.
why.sesotho: Libanka li boloka chelete e sireletsehile.

why.english: Money in the bank earns interest.

why.sesotho: Liakhaonto li ruta taolo ea chelete.
Mobile banking e etsa ditransakshene bonolo.
Libanka li fana ka litshebeletso tse sireletsehileng.
Digital banking e eketsa ho kenyelletsoa.

why.english: Understanding banking is essential for planning.

situation.english: You have M100. Should you keep it under your mattress or in a bank?
situation.sesotho: U na le M100. U e boloke kapa bankeng?

advice.english: Bank! Money in a bank is safer and earns interest.
advice.sesotho: Banka! Chelete bankeng e bolokehile le ho fumana phaello.

lesson.english: Banks are safer than keeping money at home.
lesson.sesotho: Libanka li bolokehile ho feta ho boloka chelete lapeng.

situation.english: Bank A: no monthly fee, 1% interest. Bank B: M10 monthly fee, 4% interest. You have M500. Which is better after 1 year?
situation.sesotho: Banka A: ha e lefise, 1% phaello. Banka B: M10 khoeli, 4% phaello. U na le M500. E feng e betere kamora selemo?

advice.english: Bank A: M505. Bank B: M520 - M120 fees = M400. Bank A is better for M500.
advice.sesotho: Banka A: M505. Banka B: M520 - M120 = M400. Banka A e betere.

lesson.english: Fees can eat your interest. Always calculate total cost.
lesson.sesotho: Litefiso li ka ja phaello. Dula u bala kakaretso.

situation.english: You receive M1,000 via mobile money. Transfer to bank costs M20. Is this worth it to earn 5% annual interest?
situation.sesotho: U fumana M1,000 ka mobile money. Ho romella bankeng M20. Na ho bohlokwa ho fumana 5% phaello?

advice.english: 5% on M1,000 = M50 interest. Transfer M20. Net = M30. Yes, worth it if held for a year.
advice.sesotho: 5% ho M1,000 = M50. Transfer M20. Net = M30. E, ho bohlokwa haeba e bolokilwe selemo.
